title: Choosing the Selection Control
intro: Radio for a question with one answer, checkbox for a statement or independent options, toggle only when the change applies immediately. Never pre-select.

learn.title: Six controls, six jobs
learn.text:
**Radio** — the label is a question; exactly one answer; options equally weighted; good for required input.
**Checkbox** — the label is a statement; multi-select or a single confirmation; good for optional input.
**Toggle** — a binary setting that takes effect immediately.
**Segmented** — 2–5 short options, single select.
**Dropdown** — single choice from a long list (5+).
**Chips** — short multi-select, often filters.

try.q: A settings change only takes effect after the user clicks Save. Which control is wrong for it?

left.label: Common mistakes
items: Toggle that needs a Save button

learn.title: Never pre-select
learn.text:
In usability testing, **pre-selected options are consistently overlooked and submitted unchanged**.

A pre-filled answer isn't a default the user chose — it's an answer they never gave.

Sort options from most to least common, and offer a way out: “None of the above”, “I don't remember”.

try.q: What happens to pre-selected options in testing?
options: Users overlook them and submit unchanged
Users change them more often than blank ones
try.explain: Which is why the recommendation is absolute.

learn.title: Size and layout
learn.text:
Targets around **40×40 px**.

Use a dropdown only when the list is long (5 or more) and single-choice; below that, a segmented control or radio group shows everything at once.

Chips suit short multi-select such as filters — not single-choice questions styled to look modern.

try.q: You have three mutually exclusive, short options. What should you use?
options: A segmented control or radio group
try.explain: Dropdowns hide the options; with three, show them all.

test.q: When is the label of a control a question?
test.explain: Radio: one question, exactly one answer.

test.q: What is the threshold for a dropdown?
options: Any list that doesn't fit on one line

test.q: Which control suits a single optional confirmation, such as agreeing to terms?
test.explain: The label is a statement the user agrees with or doesn't.

options: In the order the system stores them
test.explain: With a way out such as “None of the above”.
Styling radio buttons as chips is listed as a mistake.
